pairs.question: Bella etiam in Thebas, socer o pulcherrime, bella ipse paras ferroque tuos abolere nepotes? nec genus Harmoniae nec te conubia caelo festa nec hae quicquam lacrimae, furibunde, morantur? criminis haec merces? hoc fama pudorque relictus, hoc mihi Lemniacae de te meruere catenae? perge libens; at non eadem Volcania nobis obsequia, et laesi seruit tamen ira mariti! illum ego perpetuis mihi desudare caminis si iubeam uigilesque operi transmittere noctes, gaudeat ornatusque nouos ipsique laboret arma tibi; tu—sed scopulos et aena precando flectere corda paro; solum hoc tamen anxia, solum obtestor, quid me Tyrio sociare marito progeniem caram infaustisque dabas hymenaeis? dum fore praeclaros armis et uiuida rebus pectora uipereo Tyrios de sanguine inactas demissumque Iouis serie genus, a! mea quanto Sithonia mallem nupsisset uirgo sub Arcto trans Borean Thracasque tuos! indigna parumne pertulimus, diuae Veneris quod filia longum reptat et Illyricas deiectat uirus in herbas? nunc gentem inmeritam—
pairs.answer: Nec mihi Sidonii genialia foedera Cadmi nec tua cara fides (ne falsa incessere gaude!) exciderunt: prius in patrui deus infera mergar stagna et pallentes agar exarmatus ad umbras.
pairs.derivation: Venus pleads with Mars (socer), her entire address (269-291 'bella etiam... nunc gentem inmeritam') being one extended interrogative plea: why does he make war on his own offspring and has he forgotten their bonds (genus Harmoniae, conubia, Lemniacae catenae)? Quoted verbatim and contiguous; inline verse numbers 270/275/280/285/290 stripped; the conversion artifacts '++' (aposiopesis dashes at 'tu++' and the broken-off 'nunc gentem inmeritam++') rendered as em-dashes. The narrative tag 'lacrimas non pertulit ultra Bellipotens... dictisque ita mulcet amicis' (291-298) is dropped framing. Mars's reply opens with an endearment preamble 'o mihi bellorum requies... hunc ensem auellere dextrae:' (295-303) that does not answer; the answer's start is advanced to the operative sentence 'nec mihi Sidonii genialia foedera Cadmi... exarmatus ad umbras.' (300-303) which directly answers Venus's fear that he has forgotten their bond, ending at the first full stop; inline number 300 stripped. What follows the cut is 'sed nunc fatorum monitus mentemque supremi iussus obire patris...' where he turns to explaining Jupiter's compulsion and his promise of later aid.
